name: code-comparison

frames.best_why: Both panes are clear with the added and removed lines tinted, and the pointer is away from the code.

tagline: Old and new code sit side by side with red and green lines.
summary: A two-pane code viewer that shows an earlier snippet on the left and its rewrite on the right, with removed lines tinted red and added lines tinted green.
appearance: Two tall code panels share one thin-bordered dark frame. Each has a small header reading api.ts plus before or after, and a square VS badge sits between them at the centre. Code is set in a dim monospace, with a few rows washed red on the left and green on the right.
behaviour: Static: the panes do not move. Hovering one side fades and blurs the lines that are not marked as the focus of the change.
demo_content: A before and after TypeScript fetchUser function compared side by side.
search_phrases: two versions of code shown together
two code snippets next to each other
use_when: Show a refactor or migration as an old and new snippet side by side.
avoid_when: Small screens; the panes stack and long lines need horizontal scrolling.
customise: Pass beforeCode, afterCode, language, filename and the light and dark theme names, plus highlightColor; the split layout and diff tints are in the source.
weight_why: Shiki is loaded and run to highlight both snippets at runtime, then the view is static.

a11y.note: The focus blur only responds to hover, so keyboard users cannot reach it, and the low-contrast syntax colours are hard to read.

issues: The code text is very low contrast on the dark theme and hard to read.
On narrow screens the panes stack and long lines require sideways scrolling.
polish_why: Tidy diff framing and VS badge, but the code text is needlessly faint.
